summary: Disabled-by-default Gateway API HTTPRoute chart templates for messenger, mail, social, and community backbone services.
claim_boundary: This slice adds optional source-controlled Helm HTTPRoute templates and values for later cloud Gateway API integration. The routes are disabled by default and do not claim any live Gateway listener, DNS record, TLS termination, ECH publication, PQC certificate issuance, ArgoCD sync, or production route rollout.

best_practice_research.used_for: HTTPRoute as the resource that maps HTTP traffic from a Gateway listener to backend Services using hostnames, matches, filters, and backendRefs.
Gateway API role separation between Gateway infrastructure ownership and route attachment by application teams.

source_basis.use: Existing ArgoCD ApplicationSet deploys each backbone service chart into a separate namespace; HTTPRoute chart templates keep the future route seam co-located with those charts.
Existing OpenAPI server path prefixes drove the HTTPRoute pathPrefix defaults: messenger/social /api/v1 and mail/community /v1.
Existing edge hardening manifests are referenced as static TLS/ECH/PQC intent annotations without claiming live rollout.

findings: The route seam is one small Helm template per chart plus values; no runtime controller code, provider SDK, or ad-hoc templating generator was added.
The default is fail-closed via gateway.enabled=false, avoiding accidental internet exposure when the chart is installed before the pack-owned Gateway is ready.
HTTPRoute keeps application route ownership separate from the Gateway listener/TLS infrastructure owner, matching Gateway API's role-oriented model.
Each route points to the in-namespace Service and uses only the OpenAPI base path, leaving liveness/readiness probes internal to Kubernetes service checks.
Static checks assert disabled-by-default values, no wildcard hostnames, required parentRefs/backendRefs, OpenAPI/TLS/ECH/PQC annotations, and workflow path/smoke coverage for all four services.
F3_adversarial.not_applicable_reason: This is a new static chart seam rather than a defect fix; adversarial checks target accidental exposure, wildcard hostnames, missing non-claim annotations, and workflow coverage drift.
F3_adversarial.passing_fixture_id: gateway httproute static verification passed for 4 services
F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: gateway.enabled remains false and each hostname/path/contract default matches the intended OpenAPI surface.

findings: Future cloud integration can enable the route by overriding gateway.enabled and parentRef values without inventing new chart structure.
Focused Ruby checks parse all values files, assert template shape, and exercise the exact governance-smoke command now embedded in GitHub Actions.
Chose HTTPRoute chart templates over static cluster-global YAML so route ownership follows the same per-service ArgoCD chart boundary as Deployments and Services.
Chose disabled-by-default over auto-enabling in the existing dev ApplicationSet to avoid false live-route claims before DNS/Gateway/TLS evidence exists.
alternatives_named: Add static non-chart HTTPRoute YAML under cloud-iac
Enable HTTPRoute in the existing dev ApplicationSet immediately
Add disabled-by-default HTTPRoute templates to each service chart
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: The selected path is chart-ready for later cloud enablement while preserving namespace ownership and honest non-claims.
rejected_reasons: Non-chart YAML would not be applied by the existing per-service chart ApplicationSet.
Immediate enablement would imply live Gateway/DNS/TLS readiness that has not been proven.

findings: No secrets, credentials, tokens, tenant data, or certificate material were added.
No wildcard hostnames are allowed in the defaults; the route only matches the OpenAPI base path and is disabled by default.
TLS/ECH/PQC references are annotations to existing static manifests only, not embedded key material or issued certificates.
HTTPRoute metadata only affects future gateway routing; this slice adds no runtime request processing in the Rust services.
Annotations carry the audit-chain event class and OpenAPI/TLS/ECH/PQC references needed by later compliance review, but no live compliance or production control operation is claimed.
Reverting this slice removes four templates, four values blocks, CI path/smoke additions, and task/evidence text without touching service binaries, database schema, or live infrastructure.
RequestHeaderModifier sets low-cardinality X-Oyatie-Microservice and X-Oyatie-OpenAPI-Contract headers for future gateway/runtime correlation when the route is enabled.
gateway.enabled=false preserves current rendered chart behavior unless a future cloud overlay explicitly opts in.
Route names derive from existing microservice IDs and the http suffix; labels stay under existing Oyatie/Kubernetes label namespaces.
tasks/plan.md, tasks/todo.md, this multispectrum evidence, and audit-chain evidence document scope, verification, and non-claims.
Gateway templates live beside the existing per-service Helm Deployment/Service templates; no cross-layer service code changed.
Infrastructure routing metadata remains in chart/IaC files; domain, usecase, REST handler, persistence, and worker crates remain untouched.
No Cargo, npm, Helm, or provider dependency was added.
The static route schema uses Gateway API v1 HTTPRoute fields: parentRefs, hostnames, PathPrefix match, RequestHeaderModifier filter, and Service backendRefs.
Backbone CI path filters now include all four per-service Helm chart directories, and governance smoke checks the HTTPRoute template shape plus values YAML parsing.
